title: HELM-Style Holistic Evaluation
description: Holistic evaluation tests a model across many scenarios with standardized metrics instead of a single leaderboard number. Each scenario probes a different capability, and the report shows where the model is strong and where it is brittle. A capability claim is only as credible as the breadth of scenarios behind it.

demo.code:
scenarios = {"qa": 82, "summ": 77, "code": 91, "safety": 95, "reason": 68}
base = 70
passed = sum(1 for v in scenarios.values() if v >= base)
print(scenarios)
print("scenarios above baseline: %d/%d" % (passed, len(scenarios)))

title: Adversarial Prompt Probing
description: Red-team prompts try to make the model fail at its claimed capability or violate its claimed constraints. A verification suite includes hundreds of adversarial variants per claim, generated systematically rather than by hand. Claims that survive adversarial probing are far more trustworthy than those tested on friendly inputs.

demo.code:
friendly, adversarial = 100, 96
print("friendly pass rate: %d%%" % friendly)
print("adversarial pass rate: %d%%" % adversarial)
print("claim holds:", adversarial >= 95)

title: Capability Gating Tests
description: Gating tests check that a model only exercises a capability when its preconditions hold, such as refusing to answer medical questions without a disclaimer. Each gate is a paired test: the capability works in-scope and is withheld out-of-scope. Passing both directions proves the boundary is real, not decorative.

demo.code:
tests = [("in-scope", True), ("out-of-scope", False), ("in-scope", True)]
results = [got == want for (_, want), got in zip(tests, [True, False, True])]
print("paired results:", results)
print("gate verified:", all(results))

title: Statistical Significance in Benchmarks
description: A benchmark win is meaningless without confidence intervals, since small test sets produce noisy rankings. Proper verification reports the margin of error and only claims superiority when intervals do not overlap. This single practice eliminates most phantom capability claims.

demo.code:
import math
def ci(p, n):
    se = math.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n)
    return (p - 1.96 * se, p + 1.96 * se)
a, b = ci(0.82, 500), ci(0.79, 500)
print("model A 95% CI:", tuple(round(x, 3) for x in a))
print("model B 95% CI:", tuple(round(x, 3) for x in b))
print("significant:", a[0] > b[1])

title: Tool-Use Verification Sandbox
description: Claiming tool-use capability requires testing in a sandbox where tool calls are logged and their effects verified. The suite checks that the model calls the right tool with valid arguments and handles tool errors gracefully. Log inspection, not model self-report, is the evidence.

demo.code:
log = [("calc", "2+2", 4), ("search", "q", ["r1"]), ("calc", "bad(", "error")]
ok = sum(1 for t, a, r in log if r != "error")
print("tool calls:", len(log), "successful:", ok)
print("error handled gracefully:", log[2][2] == "error")

title: Long-Context Retention Tests
description: A model claiming a 128k context window must prove it uses the whole window, not just the edges. Needle-in-haystack tests hide facts at every depth and measure recall per position. The resulting heatmap shows the true effective context, which is often far shorter than the claimed window.

demo.code:
depths = [0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9]
recall = [0.98, 0.95, 0.93, 0.90, 0.88]
for d, r in zip(depths, recall): print("depth %.1f -> recall %.2f" % (d, r))
print("min recall:", min(recall), "-> claim holds:", min(recall) >= 0.9)

title: Calibration Measurement
description: A model claiming calibrated confidence must have its confidence scores match empirical accuracy. Reliability diagrams bin predictions by stated confidence and compare against actual accuracy per bin. Expected calibration error below 5 percent is the usual bar for a trustworthy claim.

demo.code:
bins = [(0.9, 0.88), (0.7, 0.72), (0.5, 0.45)]
ece = sum(abs(c - a) for c, a in bins) / len(bins)
print("bins (confidence, accuracy):", bins)
print("ECE: %.3f -> %s" % (ece, "PASS" if ece < 0.05 else "FAIL"))

title: Jailbreak Resistance Battery
description: Safety claims are verified with a battery of jailbreak techniques: roleplay, encoding tricks, multi-turn setups, and instruction hierarchy attacks. Each technique gets many variants, and the model must refuse all of them. A single bypass invalidates the absolute version of the claim.

demo.code:
attacks = {"roleplay": 0, "encoding": 0, "multiturn": 1, "hierarchy": 0}
total = sum(attacks.values())
print("bypasses per technique:", attacks)
print("claim of absolute safety:", "INVALID" if total else "holds")

title: Multilingual Capability Parity
description: A model claiming multilingual ability is tested on parallel tasks across languages, not just English. Performance drops per language reveal where the capability is real versus translated. True parity means the gap between best and worst supported language stays small.

demo.code:
scores = {"en": 88, "es": 84, "fr": 83, "sw": 71, "hi": 76}
gap = max(scores.values()) - min(scores.values())
print(scores)
print("gap:", gap, "-> parity:", "PASS" if gap < 10 else "FAIL")

title: Reasoning Trace Faithfulness
description: Chain-of-thought claims are verified by perturbing the trace and checking whether the answer changes accordingly. If the answer stays the same when the reasoning is corrupted, the trace is decorative rather than causal. Faithfulness tests separate real reasoning from rationalization.

demo.code:
orig = ("2+2=4", "4")
corrupted = ("2+2=5", "4")
faithful = corrupted[1] != orig[1]
print("original:", orig, "corrupted trace:", corrupted)
print("faithful:", faithful, "(answer should have changed)")

title: Capability Certification Checklist
description: Certification packages a claim with its evidence: test suite version, dataset hashes, environment, and raw results. An auditor can rerun the exact suite and must get the same verdict. Without this packaging, capability claims are marketing, not engineering.

demo.code:
import hashlib
suite = "cap-v3"
h = hashlib.sha256(suite.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
print("suite:", suite, "hash:", h)
print("auditor reruns suite", h, "-> same verdict required")

title: Regression Suite for Capabilities
description: Every model update reruns the capability verification suite to catch regressions. Results are tracked per version, and any drop beyond noise blocks release. Capabilities are properties of a specific model version, never of a model family in general.

demo.code:
versions = {"v1": 88.2, "v2": 89.1, "v3": 87.9}
noise = 0.5
drops = [k for k in versions if versions[k] < max(versions.values()) - noise]
print("scores:", versions)
print("regressions beyond noise:", drops or "none")

title: Human Baseline Comparison
description: Some capabilities are only meaningful relative to human performance, so verification includes a human baseline on the same tasks. The comparison uses identical instructions and scoring. Beating the baseline on the benchmark's terms is what makes the claim concrete.

demo.code:
human, model = 78.0, 83.5
print("human: %.1f  model: %.1f" % (human, model))
print("claim:", "PASS" if model >= human else "FAIL")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Human baseline', 'claim_tested': 'Human-level task skill', 'method': 'Same tasks, humans vs model', 'pass_criterion': 'Match or beat baseline', 'scope': 'Targeted', 'complexity': 'Low'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'claim_tested', 'method', 'pass_criterion', 'scope', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Compositional Generalization Tests
description: A model that learned parts should compose them in novel combinations. Verification tests unseen combinations of seen primitives, which is far harder than testing seen combinations. Passing here is strong evidence the capability is systematic rather than memorized.

title: Latency Claim Verification
description: Speed claims are verified with a standardized harness: fixed hardware, warmup runs, and percentile latencies, not cherry-picked best cases. P99 latency is reported alongside the median. A claim of real-time performance must hold at P99 under the stated load.

title: Data Contamination Checks
description: Benchmark scores are invalid if the test data leaked into training. Verification runs contamination probes: canary strings, membership inference, and near-duplicate detection against the training corpus. Contaminated results are reported as contaminated, not as capability.

demo.code:
canary = "JAH-CANARY-9f3a2b"
train_sample = "some training text without the marker"
print("canary in training:", canary in train_sample)
print("benchmark:", "VALID" if canary not in train_sample else "CONTAMINATED")

title: Refusal Boundary Mapping
description: For models that must refuse some requests and comply with others, verification maps the exact boundary with paired near-identical prompts. The map shows whether the boundary follows the policy or is arbitrary. A clean boundary map is the evidence that the policy is implemented, not just documented.

demo.code:
pairs = [("allowed v1", True), ("disallowed v1", False), ("allowed v2", True)]
got = [True, False, True]
print("boundary correct:", all(g == w for (_, w), g in zip(pairs, got)))
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Boundary mapping', 'claim_tested': 'Policy boundary', 'method': 'Paired near-identical prompts', 'pass_criterion': 'Boundary matches policy', 'scope': 'Targeted', 'complexity': 'Medium'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'claim_tested', 'method', 'pass_criterion', 'scope', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Stress-Test Capability Decay
description: Capabilities decay under long sessions, noisy inputs, and distribution shift. Verification measures the capability at increasing stress levels and plots the decay curve. A claim should state the stress level it holds at, not just the lab number.

demo.code:
stress = [0, 1, 2, 3]
score = [95, 92, 85, 70]
for s, v in zip(stress, score): print("stress", s, "->", v)
print("documented operating envelope: stress <= 2")

title: Third-Party Audit Protocol
description: The strongest verification is an independent auditor running the suite with no vendor involvement. The protocol covers auditor access, sealed test sets, and publication rules. Claims backed by third-party audits carry weight that self-reported numbers cannot.

demo.code:
audit = {"auditor": "independent", "sealed_set": True, "verdict": "confirmed"}
print("audit:", audit)
print("claim weight:", "HIGH" if audit["verdict"] == "confirmed" else "LOW")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Independent audit', 'claim_tested': 'Any major claim', 'method': 'Sealed-set third-party run', 'pass_criterion': 'Auditor confirms verdict', 'scope': 'Broad', 'complexity': 'High'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'claim_tested', 'method', 'pass_criterion', 'scope', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Ablation of Capability Sources
description: Ablation studies remove components — a tool, a retrieval index, a fine-tune — and re-measure the capability. If the score barely moves, the component was not the source of the capability. This prevents misattributing a capability to the wrong mechanism.

demo.code:
full, no_tool, no_rag = 90.0, 62.0, 85.0
print("full: %.1f  no tool: %.1f  no rag: %.1f" % (full, no_tool, no_rag))
print("capability depends mostly on:", "tool" if full - no_tool > full - no_rag else "rag")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Ablation studies', 'claim_tested': 'Capability attribution', 'method': 'Remove component, re-measure', 'pass_criterion': 'Attribution matches ablation', 'scope': 'Targeted', 'complexity': 'Medium'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'claim_tested', 'method', 'pass_criterion', 'scope', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")
